c.tagline: Balkan capital of color, coffee culture, and communist echoes.

taxi.fareNote: Metered fares are standard but confirming or negotiating a flat rate before the ride is common, especially from the airport.

emergency.note: 112 is the general EU-style emergency number that connects to police, fire, and ambulance.

hood_landmark.Komuna e Parisit: Grand Park of Tirana (Parku i Madh)

avoid.reason: Pickpocketing in the centre; usual petty-crime caution

hood_desc: The pedestrian-friendly heart of the city around Skanderbeg Square, National History Museum, and Et'hem Bey Mosque; best for first-timers who want everything walkable.

Tirana's trendiest district of leafy streets, boutiques, cafes, and nightlife, once the restricted Communist-era elite quarter; suits travelers who want upscale dining and bars within walking distance.
A quieter residential/diplomatic area near Rinia Park and the Grand Park (Parku i Madh) with the Artificial Lake; good for families and those wanting green space and calm.
An up-and-coming creative quarter near the Pyramid of Tirana and Blloku's edge, filled with street art, cafes, and design studios; suits younger travelers and digital nomads.
A traditional, budget-friendly area near the New Bazaar (Pazari i Ri) with local markets and authentic eateries; suits budget travelers wanting an authentic, less touristy feel.

water.note: Meets basic standards but aging pipes and intermittent supply mean bottled or filtered water is safer for visitors.

transit.pay: Fares are paid in cash directly to the driver or conductor on board (around 40 lek per ride); there is no rechargeable transit card system as of 2026. Exact change is appreciated.
transit.hours: Buses generally run from around 5:00 AM to midnight; no dedicated night bus network, so taxis or ride apps fill the late-night gap.
transit.note: Tirana has no metro, tram, or rail transit; buses and minibuses (furgons) are the primary public transport, supplemented by taxis and local ride-hailing apps.

train: Limited regional rail (Durrës-Tirana line under redevelopment; new Tirana-Durrës-Airport electrified line planned for 2027)
bus: Intercity furgons/minibuses to other Albanian cities

transit.m: Airport bus to city center (~40 min, hourly, 24/7)

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up the bill or leaving 5-10% at restaurants for good service is appreciated but not expected.
